purpose: Qualify scoped, source-bound fraud signals with correction, appeal, expiry and privacy constraints.

source_register.title: Positioning the SARB's Payments Ecosystem Modernisation Programme
supports: The paper proposes a future NPU baseline fraud protection capability
The paper describes participant reporting of suspected and actual fraud
The paper describes transactional fraud scoring across payment channels and participants
does_not_support: Operational nationwide fraud-sharing API
Current authority to share identified customer data
SARB endorsement of Mycelix

source_register.title: Payments Ecosystem Modernisation Programme
supports: SARB says an insights capability and fraud framework will be developed
PEM programme aims to use payments data to identify trends and combat fraud
does_not_support: A live shared fraud registry or API
Participant coverage or operational service level
Legal basis for any particular data disclosure

source_register.authority: BIS Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures / PIE Task Team 2
source_register.title: Enhancing cross-border payments — addressing fraud
supports: Fragmented data across payment networks impedes complete fraud intelligence
Privacy and regulatory differences hinder cross-border data sharing
Fraud prevention needs proportionate collaboration and coordination
does_not_support: Authority to share South African customer data
A prescribed Mycelix federated registry design
Proof that a shared global blacklist is necessary

source_register.authority: BIS Committee on Payments and Market Infrastructures / PIE Task Team 2
source_register.title: Enhancing cross-border payments: Fast Payment System interlinking
supports: Common fraud data taxonomies and data models for confirming payees are relevant to FPS interlinking
Information sharing must respect legal and policy limits
Governance and escalation roles should be clear
does_not_support: A universal cross-border fraud data permission
A requirement to share raw account or customer records

source_register.title: Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013, section 24
supports: A data subject may request correction or deletion of specified inaccurate, irrelevant, excessive, out-of-date, incomplete, misleading or unlawfully obtained personal information
Section 24(3) requires a responsible party, if reasonably practicable, to inform each recipient when a correction has an impact on decisions taken or to be taken about the data subject
Section 24(4) requires notifying the data subject who requested correction of the action taken
does_not_support: A universal number of minutes or hours for recipient cache invalidation
A requirement to disclose raw source evidence to every recipient
A universal requirement to notify every recipient when there is no decision impact

source_register.title: Protection of Personal Information Regulations, regulation 3 (amended 2025)
supports: Regulation 3 describes a right to request correction or deletion at any time and free of charge in the specified circumstances
Regulation 3.6 requires written notification to the data subject of the action taken within 30 days
does_not_support: A 30-day downstream recipient-notification or cache-invalidation SLA
A claim that all data-sharing is permitted by POPIA
A universal deadline for fraud signal recipient propagation

source_register.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Article 19
supports: Controller communicates rectification or erasure under Articles 16/17(1), or restriction under Article 18, to each recipient unless impossible or disproportionate effort
At the data subject's request, the controller informs the data subject about those recipients
does_not_support: South African legal requirements
A fixed universal recipient-propagation SLA
Authority to share data with a recipient absent a separate lawful basis
